newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH up on Guinness sale speculation.
newsitem.headline: LVMH up on Guinness sale speculation.

text.p: Shares in luxury goods group LVMH were up 2.4 percent at midday on the Paris bourse, and some brokers said the gain was partly fuelled by a report that it may sell its 20 percent stake in Guinness to eventually finance the purchase of 100 percent of duty free chain DFS.
Officials at LVMH were unavailable to comment on the report published in the weekly Nouvel Economiste.

Rumours arise frequently that LVMH may sell its Guinness stake, but the company has not signalled that it was considering such a move. Its stock rose 1.1 percent on Thursday after it announced it was taking control of the Chateau d'Yquem vineyard.
The shares were up a further 31 francs, or 2.43 percent, at 1,309 at 1140 GMT on Friday.
Last month it announced plans to buy San Francisco-based DFS for 12.6 billion francs. The deal, opposed by minority DFS partners, is currently under mediation in the United States.
